messages:
Chris (CEO): quick follow-up from the all-hands Q&A: thanks for the questions — please use this thread to surface any remaining asks about apac prewarm, autoscale fallthroughs, and customer-facing messaging.
Zara (Head of Prod): one product ask: if we add region prewarm, can teams opt into a 'soft' prewarm that warms KV cache but doesn't reserve hardware? want lower-cost option for non-enterprise customers.
Ethan (Infra Eng): short answer: yes, we planned a cache-only warm mode. implementation detail: cache-only is a lightweight pool that keeps embeddings/KV warm without pinning GPU instances. impacts: faster cold-starts but not guaranteed capacity under high surge.
Gao (Capacity): procurement note: the vendor patch we mentioned at the all-hands moves ~200 T4 slots into apac by mid-June. that's enough for base prewarm + small burst buffer, but sustained peak still requires cross-region bursting.
Nora (SRE): on autoscale rules: ops asked for a new threshold config so teams can define 'surge' vs 'sustained' load. proposing two parameters: surge_window_seconds and sustained_window_seconds. example: ``surge_window_seconds: 30, sustained_window_seconds: 600``.
Ethan (Infra Eng): we can expose those via route config in the console. also adding a rate-limiter kick-in to prevent noisy neighbor spikes from triggering cross-region moves.
Zara (Head of Prod): can we get a suggested defaults doc? most product teams won't tune this.
Nora (SRE): yes — suggested defaults: surge_window 30s, sustained_window 10m, cross_region_threshold 95th_percentile_latency > 2x baseline for 3m. will publish recommended defaults + rationale.
Gao (Capacity): cost modelling: cross-region bursts into eu for apac traffic increase egress + premium compute costs. short note for sales: estimate a 2.5x token compute multiplier during cross-region bursts for L2 models.
Chris (CEO): flag for sales: please add that multiplier to the pricing FAQ so customers see the delta when they request region-resilience.
deploy-bot: scheduled: deploy prewarm-cache-mode v0.9 -> canary 10% -> start 1765020000.
Ethan (Infra Eng): ops ask: can deploy-bot include the canary synthetic suite link? helps SRE follow regressions.
deploy-bot: updated note: canary dashboard -> https://console.internal/canaries/1765020000, synthetic suite -> prewarm_smoke_v3
Zara (Head of Prod): escalation flow question from product: in a cross-region failover, who owns customer comms? Ops or product?
Chris (CEO): ops owns immediate incident comms; product owns follow-up (customer-facing postmortem & roadmap impact). we'll codify that in the runbook.
Nora (SRE): quick technical detail: prewarm pool sizing uses 95th percentile QPS per-customer * prewarm_headroom (default 1.25). enterprise reservations skip headroom and reserve exact capacity.
Gao (Capacity): to add: we'll offer a monthly reservation API — customers can reserve X slots for Y hours/day. pricing sheet will reflect reservation discount vs on-demand.
Zara (Head of Prod): product asks for a console toggle: "prewarm: cache-only | shared-warm | reserved" with tooltip describing cost and isolation.
Ethan (Infra Eng): we'll add the toggle to the route settings page. dev note: UI flag -> routing.prewarm.mode values: ["cache_only","shared_warm","reserved"].
Chris (CEO): great. final asks: Nora + Gao, please pair on a short FAQ for customers about expected latency delta for each mode (cache-only, shared-warm, reserved). drop it here when ready.
Nora (SRE): will do — aim EOD Thursday.
Gao (Capacity): i'll include sample numbers and cost multipliers.
Zara (Head of Prod): thanks all. linking this thread into the product notes.
Chris (CEO): thanks team, closing the loop — put any follow-ups here and we'll triage. :rocket:
